newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key 182nd JGB hits record closing low of 2.180 pct.
newsitem.headline: Key 182nd JGB hits record closing low of 2.180 pct.

text.p: The benchmark 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) hit a record closing low yield of 2.180 percent on Wednesday.
The previous record closing low for any benchmark JGB was 2.205 percent on March 17.
The key 182nd JGB hit a record intra-day low yield of 2.140 percent on Wednesday, compared with Tuesday's finish at 2.255 percent.
Cash JGBs rallied after the release of the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey. The survey revealed weak sentiment at non-manufacturing and smaller firms. The June diffusion index was also weak.
Major investors including life insurers joined a buying spree during the day on the idea that the BOJ would not change its low interest rate policy in the near future, traders said.
Buying was partly fuelled by a report in the afternoon that the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau will shift its investment focus to holding JGBs for five years and longer, they said.

A MOF official told Reuters that the Bureau has more freedom in its investment now than in the previous fiscal year because given parliamentary approval, it is allowed to hold long-term JGBs it buys from the market until maturity.
"The MOF's regular buying is usually too small to give a strong impact. But many bought on this news because the sentiment was bullish," said a dealer at a Big Four brokerage.
